seo.title: Wealth Architecture & Integrated Asset Structure | DNH
seo.description: Understand how assets, ownership, obligations, liquidity, risk and objectives connect so decisions can be assessed within the whole wealth picture.

sections.heading: More assets do not necessarily create a better wealth structure
paragraphs: Wealth is more than a collection of property, gold, currencies or equities. What matters is the role each asset plays and how it connects with obligations, liquidity, risk and objectives.
DNH Wealth Architecture helps make this integrated picture clearer.

media.alt: A conceptual view of wealth architecture and connected assets

sections.heading: Asset variety does not always mean the structure is right
sections.intro: You may have built valuable holdings over time while their combined structure no longer fits your financial needs and objectives.

items.title: Unclear asset roles
items.description: It is not clear whether each investment is held for growth, income or value preservation.

items.title: Capital concentration
items.description: A large share of wealth is exposed to one asset or market.

items.title: Fragmented decisions
items.description: Investments were made at different times without reference to the whole structure.

items.title: Liquidity mismatch
items.description: Asset values are high, but access to cash is difficult when it is needed.

items.title: Misalignment with objectives
items.description: The current asset mix does not align with future needs and plans.

sections.heading: Wealth architecture means seeing how every financial component connects
sections.intro: Asset values alone do not describe the true wealth position. Ownership, debts, obligations, cash flows and financial objectives also need to be viewed together.

items.title: Assets
items.description: Which assets do you own, and how is capital distributed between them?

items.title: Ownership
items.description: How are personal, family and business assets owned and related?

items.title: Debts and obligations
items.description: Which financial responsibilities and future payments lie ahead?

items.title: Cash flow and liquidity
items.description: Where do funds come from, and how much capital is available when required?

items.title: Risks
items.description: Which assets or economic factors could affect different parts of wealth?

items.title: Objectives and time horizon
items.description: Does the current structure fit today’s needs and long-term plans?

sections.closing: Wealth architecture clarifies these relationships so that decisions can be reviewed against the whole financial position.
sections.note: Ownership is considered through its financial implications. Legal, tax or formal ownership restructuring is outside this review unless separately agreed and appropriately qualified.

sections.heading: Every asset has a role beyond its standalone value
sections.heading_highlight: a role beyond its standalone value
sections.intro: An asset should not be reviewed through value or return alone. Its contribution to capital preservation, income, liquidity and risk also matters.

items.title: Currencies
items.description: Understand currency exposure and the effect of exchange-rate change on wealth.

items.title: Gold
items.description: Review its possible value-preservation role and economic risks without assuming certain protection or return.

items.title: Property
items.description: Assess the role of property in wealth, income and liquidity.

items.title: Equities
items.description: Review growth potential alongside volatility and concentration risk.

items.title: Cash
items.description: Maintain access to funds for obligations and future opportunities.

items.title: Fixed income
items.description: Review periodic income alongside credit, inflation and liquidity risks relevant to the instrument.

items.title: Alternative assets
items.description: Assess their fit with objectives, risk tolerance and financial needs.

items.title: Business and private investment
items.description: Review connections between business capital, personal assets and shared risks.

sections.heading: When does a wealth-structure review become more important?
sections.intro: As assets, obligations and financial decisions become more complex, an integrated view of wealth becomes increasingly valuable.

items.title: An important financial decision lies ahead
items.description: Before buying, selling or moving capital, understand the effect on total wealth.

items.title: You own diverse assets
items.description: Capital is held across several markets, but the relationships are not clear.

items.title: You have different financial objectives
items.description: Value preservation, capital growth, liquidity and family plans need to work together.

items.title: Your capital is highly concentrated
items.description: A substantial share of wealth depends on one asset, market or business.

sections.heading: The DNH approach: understand today with the future in view
sections.intro: Developed from Dr Nasim Mohammadhassani’s analytical perspective, the DNH Framework rests on three ideas: understand the current position, examine decision options and keep long-term objectives in view.

items.label: D | DATA INTELLIGENCE
items.title: Data Intelligence
items.description: Understand the data, assets and financial factors shaping the current position.

items.label: N | NAVIGATION STRATEGY
items.title: Navigation Strategy
items.description: Examine decision options, constraints and risks.

items.label: H | HORIZON ARCHITECTURE
items.title: Horizon Architecture
items.description: Align today’s decisions with future needs and objectives.

sections.eyebrow: From structure to matters requiring review
sections.heading: Clarify the current wealth picture before making a new decision
sections.intro: Wealth architecture begins with the existing structure. Its purpose is to clarify relationships and the matters that should be examined before an important decision.

sections.heading: Wealth architecture considers decisions within the whole financial position
paragraphs: This approach helps examine the relationship between assets, risks, liquidity and objectives; it does not guarantee returns or replace the client’s responsible decision-making.

sections.heading: Understand your wealth structure before changing assets
paragraphs: If you own diverse assets or face an important financial decision, an initial assessment can help clarify the position and identify the central issues.
Where appropriate, a specialist review path can be defined after that initial understanding.
sections.closing: Banking information and confidential asset details are not required at the first stage.
